content.text:
Five feature groups fit the current frontend.

- Search entry and clearing. Use `getByRole("searchbox", { name: "Search MPs and funders" })` or `#entity-search`. Idle examples are buttons named `John` and `HSBC`. `/` focuses the input; Enter submits immediately; Escape while the input is focused clears it. `Clear search` removes `q`, returns to the `Start with a name` heading and focuses the input. Queries require three trimmed Unicode characters and otherwise show `Type N more character(s) to search.` [App.svelte](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/src/App.svelte:161).

- Threshold and URL restoration. Use `getByRole("slider", { name: "Similarity threshold" })` or `#similarity-threshold`; `.threshold-label output` shows two decimals. Range is `0..1`, step `0.01`, default `1`. Load `/?q=John&strictness=0.65` to restore both controls. Changes use `replaceState`, so they do not create browser-history entries. `popstate` rereads both parameters. Invalid strictness falls back to `1`; valid values round to two decimals. [App.svelte](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/src/App.svelte:87), [search.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/src/lib/search.ts:11).

- Loading, cancellation and recovery. Use `getByRole("region", { name: "Search results" })` with `aria-busy`, heading `Searching`, and `getByRole("status")` for announcements. Errors expose `getByRole("alert")`, heading `Search couldn’t load`, and button `Try again`. Empty results expose heading `No matches for “TERM”` and `Edit your search`, which focuses and selects the input. Typing debounces 250 ms; retry bypasses debounce; timeout is 10 seconds. Cleanup aborts previous requests and prevents stale responses from replacing current results. [App.svelte](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/src/App.svelte:40), [search.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/src/lib/search.ts:51).

- Result fidelity and entity context. Use `.entity-row`, `.entity-name`, `.entity-name mark`, `.entity-kind-label`, `.entity-kind`, `.entity-icon`, and `.entity-tooltip`. Headings report `N result(s) shown`. Names preserve response ordering, spelling and duplicates. Buttons have accessible names such as `MP`, `Funder: Company` and `Funder: Individual`. Focus or hover exposes the tooltip; Escape dismisses it. Funders show subtype labels; MPs do not. Ten entries of either kind trigger `.results-note`. Rows are display items, without entity navigation. [App.svelte](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/src/App.svelte:301), [EntityIndicator.svelte](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/src/lib/EntityIndicator.svelte:35).

- Keyboard, literal text and narrow layout. Existing tests offer reusable assertions for focus, tooltip dismissal, regex/HTML-like names, and horizontal overflow at `360×780`. The skip link targets `#search`; the home link has accessible name `Exposed home`. [search.spec.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/tests/search.spec.ts:165), [App.svelte](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/src/App.svelte:148).

The real request is `/api/search?term=John&max_entries=10&strictness=1`. Vite strips `/api` and forwards to Rust `/search`, defaulting to `http://127.0.0.1:6999`; set `EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN` before Vite starts for the worktree API port. `max_entries` caps each entity type separately, so up to 20 combined results is legitimate. [search.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/src/lib/search.ts:67), [vite.config.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/vite.config.ts:4).

The existing Playwright command is `npm --prefix frontend test`, with Chromium installed using `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0`. Its config launches Vite dev on fixed port `4173`, uses Desktop Chrome, retains failed traces, and reuses an existing server outside CI. That reuse can silently target another checkout or another API origin. The config does not launch Rust or PostgreSQL. Worktree Compose ports come from `.env.compose`, so neither `4173` nor `6999` should be assumed for an already-running worktree environment. [package.json](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/package.json:16), [playwright.config.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/playwright.config.ts:9), [README.md](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/README.md:127).

Every existing browser test intercepts `**/api/search?*` and fulfills a fabricated response. They prove frontend behavior against controlled inputs, including fabricated ranking. A real-backend verification must omit those routes, observe the actual browser response, and compare its `entities` with rendered names and kind labels. Known examples such as `HSBC` depend on imported data. No live backend behavior was exercised in this read-only investigation. [search.spec.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/frontend/tests/search.spec.ts:16), [README.md](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-verification-skill-20261006/README.md:201).
